name: Budapest School
summary: The Budapest School was a circle of Hungarian philosophers around Georg Lukács, including Ágnes Heller, Ferenc Fehér, György Márkus and Mihály Vajda, that began as Marxist humanism and moved toward post-Marxist radical democracy. It revived the early Marx's themes of alienation and radical needs, condemned Soviet-type societies as totalitarian 'dictatorships over needs', and held that socialism cannot exist without democracy and pluralism. Later members accepted markets, the welfare state and constitutional rights, and largely abandoned orthodox Marxist economics.
scope: The Budapest School of c. 1963 to the mid-1980s and the later views of its core members (Heller, Fehér, Márkus), drawing on Dictatorship over Needs (1983), Heller's Theory of Need in Marx (1976) and her 1999 Radical Philosophy interview. It excludes Lukács's own orthodox period and the looser associates who became dissident liberals. Most answers on modern policy are inferred from principles, so many are low confidence.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Heller's endorsement of the welfare state as the best redistributive tool and her concern for equality; no source discusses inheritance tax.

basic-income.rationale: Heller favoured welfare redistribution but criticised its quantified, individualist form; adherents have no documented stance on unconditional income, so it is genuinely open.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the school's turn toward market-compatible managed capitalism and Nordic-style models rather than protectionism; the sources never address tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The school held that Soviet-type planning was inefficient and accepted neoclassical critiques of it, so state direction of investment is inferred to be unwelcome.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The school accepted markets and mixed economies but never discussed property distribution; inferred as split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Later members largely discarded traditional Marxist economics and accepted market links to freedom, so abolishing money and wages is inferred to be rejected.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The school analysed mixed economies of modern capitalism as workable; nothing suggests abolishing central banks, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from Heller's pluralist, anti-statist stance and preference for representation with safeguards; state-recognised corporate bodies cut against pluralism.

one-party-rule.rationale: Fehér, Heller and Márkus argued that Soviet-type one-party rule is totalitarian because it suppresses pluralism, and that socialism cannot be conceived without democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred: Heller held democracy is not the only modern form and valued Hume-style liberalism, but the school's commitments are republican and secular; monarchy is never discussed.

democracy-best.rationale: Heller said "pure democracy without safeguards is pure terror" and that democracy is not the only modern political form, so she endorses democracy with safeguards but not as an absolute.

direct-votes.rationale: Heller favoured representation alongside participation and warned that pure democracy without safeguards is terror, which counts against replacing representatives with direct votes.

workers-councils.rationale: The school praised 1956 Hungary, whose workers' councils featured in it, but later favoured representative democracy; adherents split on councils as the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Heller said nations have a right not to be interfered with, but secession of regions is never addressed; left neutral.

natural-rulers.rationale: Heller's ethics opposed doctrines denying equality, rationality and self-determination, so a natural hierarchy of rulers is rejected.

political-violence-never.rationale: Heller held that after 1968 no political revolution is needed yet called 1956 a socialist revolution; adherents are not pacifists but no stance on absolutes is documented.

war-builds-character.rationale: Heller's ethics grew from the Holocaust and totalitarianism and stress human dignity, so glorifying war is rejected.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from Heller's secular, modern liberal outlook and pluralism; religion and the state are not directly discussed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Heller's modern pluralist and autonomy-based ethics reject laws derived from scripture; inferred from principles rather than stated.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The school wanted democratic public institutions and safeguards for rights; privatised courts and defence conflict with this.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the school's critique of Soviet-bloc domination and focus on democratisation, not military primacy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism and totalitarian group claims and argued for an open, pluralistic society, so an ethnically defined nation is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Heller rejected economic necessitarianism and a necessary path of history, so class conflict as the main driver is rejected.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Heller favoured welfare redistribution and equality of dignity but rejected dictating real needs; equal outcomes is inferred as too strong.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources for a stance.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources on the school never discuss colonial reparations, so no position can be stated and it is left neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from Heller's criticism of nationalism and fundamentalism and her pluralist universalism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Heller's critique of the capitalist need to have and her ethics treating persons as ends suggest rejecting self-interest as morally good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Heller defended negative liberties as basic to the modern state and opposed collective claims overriding persons, so duties before rights is rejected.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Heller's concern for needs and environmental limits is noted, but intrinsic value of nature is not a documented position.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal personal-autonomy commitments that coercive limits are unwelcome.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Heller held modernity is a lasting condition ("a world in which we are born") to be lived with, not negated, so calling it a disaster is rejected.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Heller rejected the technological imagination as dominant and sought balance; accelerating disruption is inferred as unwelcome.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no documented position.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from Heller's opposition to experts or functionaries deciding people's real needs for them.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the school's anti-totalitarian defence of privacy and freedom from state control.

restore-past-order.rationale: Heller treated modernity as irreversible and rejected nostalgic restoration; her thought is forward-looking critical theory.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Heller's theory is explicitly principled and philosophical; judging only by results is inferred as foreign to it.

direct-action.rationale: Heller said no political revolution is needed and favoured democratic safeguards and movements for social justice working within pluralism.

means-match-ends.rationale: Heller's Kantian objection to treating persons as mere means and her stress on self-legislating democracy imply methods should match aims; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Modernity is affirmed as an inescapable condition; foraging is never entertained.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Heller said she preferred the term functional division of labour for modern society and treated it as a lasting feature of modernity.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Heller's theory of needs rejects a dictatorship over real needs and says satisfying all needs is a romantic position, so distribution by a central standard of need is contested.

production-for-use.rationale: Heller's needs theory criticises production geared to the need to have, yet she accepted market economies; adherents are split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The school largely discarded traditional Marxist economics, including labour-theory exploitation, so this is rejected as stated.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorship over Needs condemns Soviet-type rule as totalitarian and holds socialism inconceivable without democracy, which rules out dictatorial working-class power.

collective-farming.rationale: Fehér, Heller and Márkus condemned Soviet-style systems; collective farming as a project of those regimes is rejected.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The school largely discarded classical Marxist economics and theories of imperialism; not stated, inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Heller called the welfare state the best redistributive tool; taxation as theft is contrary to her view.

harm-principle.rationale: Heller admired the British liberal tradition and Berlin, and defended negative liberties; a harm-principle limit on the state is inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Heller's ethics oppose group interests overriding persons and defend negative liberties as rights of individuals, though she called rights abstractions.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal commitments to personal autonomy.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The school's core claim is that democratic participation and pluralism are essential, so exit as a substitute for voting is rejected.

state-as-business.rationale: Heller criticised treating persons as means and turning ends into means; running the state as a business customers can leave conflicts with it.

positive-liberty.rationale: Heller's theory of needs treats freedom as including the means of satisfying radical needs; the school shifted from capitalism's need-to-have to enabling material freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; Heller was herself an academic and no source supports this claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Heller's ethics grew from the Holocaust and rejects racial hierarchies; stated through her opposition to doctrines denying equality. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

organic-representation.rationale: Heller wanted representation with safeguards for individual rights; estate-style organic bodies cut against modern pluralism.

total-state.rationale: The review of Dictatorship over Needs reports that the authors treat state control over all spheres, including needs, as the totalitarian core of Soviet-type societies.

national-rebirth.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism and fundamentalism and rejected totalitarian mobilisation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Heller held that nations have the right not to be interfered with, which rules out expansionism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Pre-modern vassal rule is incompatible with Heller's affirmation of modern constitutional democracy.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom contradicts the school's commitment to personal autonomy and freedom from domination.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Heller held that Marxism had plural, personal forms and accepted a postmodern perspective on modernity, but defended universal ethics; split.

universal-morality.rationale: Heller's ethics sought grounding in human substance and relative autonomy; she held universal ethical claims while rejecting absolutes.

single-common-good.rationale: The school argued that parties claiming to represent a single universal interest are totalitarian and that pluralism must be protected.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Heller came from a Jewish family but is not documented as taking a position on Israel; left neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights never come up in the school's writings on needs, totalitarianism or democracy; left neutral.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival policy is outside the school's concerns; Heller's anti-nationalism gives no clear direction, so neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Heller's theory of radical needs and self-governance favour more democratic participation in economic life; the school supported self-managing socialism.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not discussed in any source on Heller or the school, so there is no basis for a position.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of managed Nordic-style capitalism, where stimulus is accepted.

economic-freedom.rationale: The school accepted a link between markets and freedom but also held that capitalism and democracy can come apart; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Heller defended constitutional safeguards and rights, not rule by moral example of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: The school drew from 1956 the lesson that socialism must be applied differently in each nation, and Heller called 1956 a war of independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Heller's remarks on non-interference and rights give no clear line on UN authorisation for force; left neutral.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Heller favoured pluralism and said Marxism resembled Christianity in forms of personal faith; reason as the only guide is not her position.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from Heller's universalist ethics of equal moral worth.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Heller supported the welfare state as best redistribution while criticising its quantification; work tests are inferred as unwelcome.

class-collaboration.rationale: Not addressed; Heller rejected class struggle as history's driver but did not endorse corporatist partnership.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Heller as a philosopher of culture and modernity prized cultural heritage; sacrificing institutions is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's critique of bloc politics.

workers-nation.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism, and the school moved away from class-based national organisation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Heller supported female quotas and wrote that she studied science to show women are as good as men.

ban-interest.rationale: The school accepted modern market economies where credit and interest exist.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Heller said her ethics oppose theories that deny equality, and her moral thought arose from the experience of the Holocaust, so legal racial segregation is firmly rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Heller described Soviet-type regimes as a distinct totalitarian form and favoured constitutional democracy; the instrumental state theory was abandoned.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from Heller's criticism of consumer society and concern for needs; fossil fuels are never discussed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Heller advocated an open, pluralistic society where people shape identities, which counts against enforced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Heller opposed nationalism and fundamentalism, and conspiracy theories of this kind are foreign to her thought.

proportional-representation.rationale: Heller favoured representation and pluralism; PR is inferred as consistent but never discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism and totalitarian missions.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Heller backed female quotas and criticised gender inequality but was critical of some current feminism; moderate support inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not a documented position; adherents criticised Orbán's government but not elites in general.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Heller's ethics was built in response to Nazi crimes and rejects treating persons as means, so eugenic state limits are firmly rejected.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Heller's concern with totalitarian crimes and her defence of constitutional rights imply support for legal accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Heller endorsed the welfare state as the best redistributive tool, so a minimal state is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Heller's thought was shaped by the Holocaust and opposes racial hierarchy, so discouraging cross-racial marriage is rejected.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Heller's mature ethics opposed theories denying equality and made the individual and human substance the source of the good.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The school argued Soviet states were totalitarian rather than socialist and wanted national roads to socialism, so the one-country thesis is rejected in this form.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The school did not write on settler colonialism, so adherents have no documented stance.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from Heller's equality before the law and individual rights, though not discussed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Heller's personal autonomy and negative-liberty defence rules out restricting conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal pluralism and opposition to religion-based legislation.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from secular liberal outlook; religious instruction in schools is never discussed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The review reports that the authors saw strengthened party-state control as the mark of totalitarian Soviet-type regimes, not of socialism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Heller favoured democracy with representation, and the review reports socialism cannot be conceived without democracy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are inferred as unwelcome given the school's embrace of markets.

population-transfer.rationale: Heller's moral philosophy grew out of the Holocaust and totalitarianism and holds that persons are ends; forced removal of minorities is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist claims about peoples contradict Heller's ethics of equality and dignity.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Heller held democracy needs safeguards but stressed pluralism and free dissent; adherents likely split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Heller opposed any dictatorship over needs and domination by officials deciding real needs, which fits freedom as non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Heller held pure democracy without safeguards is terror, and defended constitutional rights and institutions.

vanguard-party.rationale: The review shows the authors condemn Soviet-type party rule and the party's claim to represent universality, rejecting a vanguard party. The sources do not state this position outright; it follows from the tradition's core commitments.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from Heller's support for the welfare state as redistribution.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is never discussed by the school; neutral.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the school's support for independent organisation and pluralism.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's attention to social institutions and needs structures.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Heller argued for an open pluralistic society where people shape identities, which rejects the claim.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; Heller favoured elected representation.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Heller defended negative liberties as basic to the modern state and warned of terror; suspending them is rejected.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; accepted markets but supported welfare protection.

party-controls-media.rationale: The review says the authors treated suppression of pluralism and independent opinion as defining Soviet-type totalitarianism, so party control of media is rejected. The sources do not state this position outright; it follows from the tradition's core commitments.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the army belongs to the Soviet-type model the authors condemned.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from Heller's open, pluralist society and critique of nationalism.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The school did not discuss the pay of elected officials; neutral.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from the school's criticism of party-state monolithism; it favoured pluralism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism and supported Europe as a democratic project; inferred from that, not stated directly.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from separation of powers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not a topic in the sources on the school; neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: Heller criticised fundamentalism and defended pluralism and personal autonomy, so rule by religious scholars is firmly rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Leninist doctrine the school never discussed or adopted; left neutral.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The review says the authors treated suppression of independent opinion as totalitarian; censoring art conflicts with this.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from the safeguards Heller said democracy needs.

recall-officials.rationale: Heller favoured representation alongside participation; recall is not discussed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The school criticised Soviet hegemony but never took a stance on alliances generally; neutral.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from acceptance of market economies.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal safeguards.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Heller treated modernity as a world to live in, not to flee; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Partition and reunification are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The school was an intellectual circle; inferred rejection of anti-intellectual claims.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Heller held universalist ethics while accepting plural forms of life; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from Heller's ethics of human dignity and the Holocaust-rooted moral inquiry.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Heller supported gender equality measures like quotas; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from modern secular rationalism; creationism in schools is not discussed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from Heller's defence of negative liberties, which weighs against legal restriction of adult material.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from Heller's criticism of nationalism and open society.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the school's pluralism and defence of minorities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities are not discussed; Heller's pluralism and equality before the law pull both ways.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Heller held it is possible to choose yourself and that people shape their identities, in line with the Millian idea; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Post-colonial economics falls outside the school's documented writings; neutral.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the school's democratic commitments and its praise of the 1956 revolution.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The review notes that the authors condemned Soviet-type regimes that suppressed pluralism and freedom, and said socialism cannot be conceived without democracy.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from Heller's universalist ethics and welfare support.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear deterrence policy is not addressed in the sources on the school.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The school's writing gives no view on how heads of state should be chosen; neutral.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank design is not discussed by the school; neutral.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from Heller's criticism of nationalism and historical territorial claims.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Heller's theory of needs and criticism of the need to have imply property is not absolute; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The authors described Soviet-type systems as a new kind of totalitarian dictatorship over needs, not as state capitalism, though they denied they were socialist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees are not discussed by the school; neutral.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Heller held nations have the right not to be interfered with, and the school rejected Soviet hegemony in Hungary.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from liberal pluralism, which opposes both church power and state control of religion.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the school's democratic and self-determination commitments.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-region autonomy arrangements are not discussed in the school's writings; neutral.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Heller's modern secular ethics and anti-totalitarian writings reject sacralised rulers; leader cults belong to the regimes she condemned.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from support for welfare-state redistribution.

character-from-environment.rationale: Heller emphasised social formation of needs and human substance; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Heller said democracy needs safeguards and defended constitutional rights, which rejects a ruler above law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Heller's scepticism about technological imagination.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not part of the school's documented positions; neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: The review describes Soviet-type regimes as totalitarian, and the authors condemn the cult of party and leader as part of the dictatorship over needs.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are not discussed by the school; neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The authors saw party elites as a new ruling stratum, but the doctrine of continuing class struggle is Maoist, not theirs; split.

land-redistribution.rationale: Agrarian land reform is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the school's human-rights liberalism.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism, so claims over territory on ethnic grounds are rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Heller defended negative liberties and personal choice, which rule out penalising apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Heller's defence of individual liberty and equality of women rejects compulsory covering.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed in the sources on the school; neutral.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from Heller's criticism of nationalism and ethnic politics.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not specifically discussed by the school; neutral.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Diaspora political strategy is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Heller rejected economic necessitarianism and any necessary path of history while treating needs as important.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the school's acceptance of a regulated mixed economy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from the school's welfare-state outlook.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Heller said pure democracy without safeguards is terror, so courts must constrain majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Heller joined a campaign for a female quota in Hungary's legislature.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs are alien to the school's modern liberal outlook.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from welfare and needs-based concerns.

moral-incentives.rationale: The review says Soviet-type regimes use dictatorship over needs; replacing material incentives with imposed moral ones is not endorsed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Heller said no political revolution is needed and rejected violent vanguardism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Heller's ethics of equality opposes hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from Heller's criticism of nationalism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Heller's ethics of equal dignity and self-determination reject rule over so-called less advanced peoples.

patriotic-education.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism, so state-mandated pride in nation is inferred as unwelcome.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The school wrote nothing on affirmative action, and adherents' equality ethics and wariness of group claims pull in opposite directions.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform of this kind is not discussed by the school; neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The school analysed modern mixed economies as durable and largely discarded Marxist collapse theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from the school's critique of Soviet domination.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from the school's acceptance of market links to freedom.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Lenin's labour-aristocracy thesis is not discussed in the sources on the school, which largely dropped Marxist economics.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Heller's equality ethics reject a right to discriminate; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Heller defended constitutional rights as the guarantee of negative liberties and warned against unrestrained democracy.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era treaty law is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

elective-rulers.rationale: Elected rulers fit the school's democratic commitments.

minority-veto.rationale: Heller favoured representation and safeguards for individuals, not a veto for each member over collective decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from Heller's praise of 1956 and her view that regimes breaching legitimate order can be resisted.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Heller wanted safeguards limiting any majority, so parliamentary supremacy is not endorsed as such; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as a standard modern humane commitment.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in the school's writing; neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Heller grounded welfare in equality and rights rather than aristocratic duty; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The school stressed participation and democratic engagement as central to a good society.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Heller criticised consumer society and manipulation of needs in advanced capitalism as of utmost importance to resist.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed directly; Heller viewed consumer manipulation as part of this but did not adopt Gramscian terms.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is outside the school's documented concerns, which focused on Soviet-type and Western societies.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from Heller's open, pluralist society and opposition to nationalism.

party-own-road.rationale: The 1956 experience led Lukács, Heller and others to hold that socialism had to be applied differently in each nation.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from Heller's criticism of nationalism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous political leadership is not discussed by the school; neutral.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Heller's thought arose from the Holocaust and opposition to totalitarianism; inferred support.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Dictatorship over Needs and the school's later work describe Soviet-type societies as totalitarian, which leans toward the statement, but the cited review does not show them condemning fascism and communism together as equivalent.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from standard historical consensus.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Public memorial disputes are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Heller was sceptical of some current feminism but did not write on male disadvantage; neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources on the school give no view on the comparative seriousness of domestic violence by sex; neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Heller held modernity is a shared world condition and defended universal liberties.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the school's commitment to constitutional democracy and civil control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic labour are not discussed in the sources on Heller or the school; neutral.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial obligations are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not discussed by the school; neutral.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from Heller's emphasis on personal autonomy and choosing yourself.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Heller favoured representation with safeguards rather than binding mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from Heller's support for the welfare state.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of mixed economies.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from Heller's support for representation and safeguards.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from pluralism and criticism of nationalism.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the open, anti-nationalist outlook.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal tests for indirect discrimination are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Heller criticised consumer society as much as Eastern Bloc dictatorships and described capitalism as turning needs into an endless need to have.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Heller's rejection of interference in nations.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The school's formative experience was the Soviet crushing of Hungary in 1956 and Czechoslovakia in 1968, which turned it against such interventions.

corporate-influence.rationale: Heller's critique of capitalism's turning needs into means and of manipulation of needs implies concern about corporate influence.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the school's defence of free civil society.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth policy is not discussed by the school; neutral.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from open liberalism.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employer-of-last-resort schemes are not discussed; Heller backed welfare redistribution but not this device.

democratic-peace.rationale: The democratic-peace thesis is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Heller saw obedience as bound to legitimate, democratic order; adherents split.

non-intervention.rationale: Heller said nations have the right not to be interfered with yet also valued human rights. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not a topic in the sources on the school; neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about minorities contradict Heller's Holocaust-rooted ethics and her opposition to antisemitism, which she saw in 1950s Hungarian trials.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the school's opposition to the party-state's control of information.

local-production.rationale: Localist economics is not addressed by the school; neutral.

informal-organisation.rationale: Affinity-group organising is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from Heller's support for rights beyond the nation-state.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The school's experience under Soviet hegemony and its judgement of 1956 as a war of independence reject ritual submission to a leading power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Heller accepted personal property and criticised Soviet control over needs, so personal belongings staying private is inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: The authors opposed Soviet-type systems but also held that they would collapse and could not be reformed; no stance on a crusade.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The school accepted mixed economies, including Nordic-style managed capitalism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Heller likened Marxism to a plural personal faith and did not make a stance on religion; split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Heller viewed capitalism as a modern logic with its own tendencies yet impoverishing; split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources give Heller's support for gender equality but no view on whether it depends on economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework and childcare is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from anti-nationalism and open culture.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with indigenous nations are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Heller's radical needs emphasise community and self-governance but she accepted modern complex society; split.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the open, pluralist society and rejection of nationalism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Heller criticised consumer capitalism as much as Soviet-bloc dictatorship, while seeking a third way of radical democracy.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the school's criticism of nationalism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Heller's father died at Auschwitz and her ethical inquiry grew out of the Holocaust, so denial is categorically rejected.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Heller's defence of negative liberties and individual autonomy rules out criminalising private sexual relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The review says suppression of pluralism is what makes Soviet-type regimes totalitarian, so suppressing opposition is rejected.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Heller defended negative liberties and plural beliefs, which rule out punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from her ethics of equal dignity and self-determination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islamic jurisprudence on jihad is outside the school's documented concerns; neutral.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Heller criticised fundamentalism and defended pluralism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Heller favoured representation alongside participation, so participation is supported but not as a replacement.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Heller was critical of some contemporary feminism and did not adopt intersectionality; split.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Heller's support for personal autonomy and equality.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical end-of-life policy is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; Heller identified with a different kind of Marxist while moving beyond orthodoxy.

alienated-labor.rationale: Márkus and Heller revived the early Marx's concept of alienation as a central critique of capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Heller criticised fundamentalism and nationalism but defended pluralism; incompatibility claims about a religion are rejected.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Heller's modern secular democratic outlook rejects divine sources of authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not discussed in the sources; Heller's pluralism and secularism pull both ways.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from Heller's rights-based outlook that confidentiality gagging of harassment claims would be disfavoured; not stated.

social-market-economy.rationale: The school treated Nordic managed capitalism as a model and accepted the link between markets and freedom.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as a utopian position the school did not take.

rich-first.rationale: Deng-style uneven development is not discussed by the school; neutral.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; the school opposed the Soviet bloc but took no stated stance on neutrality.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from acceptance of modern markets.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Debt conditionality is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

property-franchise.rationale: Heller's democratic commitments and ethics of equality reject limiting the vote by property.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claims are not discussed by Heller or the school; neutral.

reification.rationale: The school's Lukácsian heritage centres on reification, though later members largely moved away from traditional Marxist economics.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed; Heller criticised capitalist manipulation of needs but valued free press.

racial-franchise.rationale: Heller's ethics of equality and Holocaust-rooted moral thought reject racial limits on the vote.

online-participation.rationale: Digital democracy is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the school's opposition to party-state secrecy and control of information.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Heller's defence of personal autonomy and equality rejects restricting marriage by religion. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Heller's moral thought grew from the Holocaust and rejects such boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition-based deliberation is not discussed in the sources; Heller favoured representation but also participation.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Heller's pluralist outlook and view that doctrines take plural personal forms.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Heller's critique of capitalism's logic of having and her view that democracy and capitalism can diverge imply concern; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the equality and autonomy commitments.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The review describes the authors condemning the Soviet-type state's suppression of pluralism and independent belief, which includes state-imposed atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Heller defended constitutional order and safeguards, not abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational arrangements are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Heller called the welfare state the best redistributive tool, though she criticised its loneliness.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from preference for representation with safeguards.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential-risk policy is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from Heller's gender equality commitments.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from Heller's commitment to gender equality, which implies marital authority should be shared.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Non-citizen voting is not discussed in the sources; Heller's open-society outlook pulls one way, representation theory the other.

rent-control.rationale: Rent regulation is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from acceptance of mixed markets.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Regimented mass youth movements belong to the totalitarian pattern the authors analysed and condemned.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing of nuclear weapons is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The school opposed Soviet domination of Hungary, but foreign bases in general are not discussed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from Heller's moral focus on the Holocaust and crimes of totalitarianism.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The school moved away from labour-based Marxist economics, so split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; pacifism is not part of the school.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism, and myths of unbroken ancient national continuity belong to the nationalist narratives she opposed.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The constructedness of sex is not discussed in the sources on Heller or the school; neutral.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Heller was critical of some current feminism but did not take a stance on this.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Heller's criticism of nationalism, which includes the sacralising of national sacrifice.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Heller defended pluralism and warned against absolutist claims in politics.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The cultural-centre role of a homeland is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural-nationalist sequencing is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological language is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of ethnic nationalism and from equality ethics.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative boundaries for peoples are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

independent-unions.rationale: The school's formative reference was 1956 Hungary and its rejection of the party-state's control of society, so unions free of the ruling party are supported.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The authors held that Soviet-type societies were not socialist because they lacked democracy, but held socialism cannot exist without democracy more broadly than workers' power. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from Heller's support for the welfare state.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative structure is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership is not discussed in the sources; the school accepted mixed economies, so a mild lean is inferred at most.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Confederal municipalism is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

family-wage.rationale: Wage-setting for family support is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Payment privacy is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the school's defence of freedom against state control.

person-over-state.rationale: Heller's ethics made the individual and human substance the source of the good and opposed theories that subordinate persons to group interests.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Heller compared Marxism to plural, personal faith but the sources give no view on a spiritual human nature; neutral.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Constitutional design for regional autonomy is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Heller's ethics oppose theories that deny equality and place group interests above persons.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from her opposition to group-based claims.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Military doctrine is not discussed by the school; neutral.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Defining nations by language is part of the nationalist thinking Heller criticised; inferred from that criticism.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the individual-rights and equality commitments.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiratorial nationalism is rejected by Heller.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition policy is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Heller's concern with distinguishing essential from artificial needs and with scarcity suggests support; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as consistent with her ethics.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Heller was critical of some feminism and her ethics treats persons as individuals.

arms-reduction.rationale: Arms control is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret diplomacy is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of market economies.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from her view that rights depend on constitutions and the state.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Conscientious refusal in wars between states is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from Heller's support for the welfare state and independent organisation.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credit design is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: International economic order reform is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Heller said no political revolution is needed and defended constitutional safeguards, so smashing the state is rejected.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Economic pluralism between communities is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Heller criticised the capitalist logic of making ends into means, which counts against pricing nature as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism and fundamentalism as totalising claims.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Internal-colonialism theory is not discussed by the school; neutral.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Heller's ethics took human substance as the source of the good and universal dignity.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from support for independent institutions and the welfare state.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Perennialism is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Heller's equality ethics and support for women's equality, including female quotas, firmly back equal property rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language-naming disputes are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Environmental liability law is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the democratic and representative commitments.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Heller defended negative liberties as basic to the modern state, so overriding them for environmental aims is disfavoured.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the concern for judges and safeguards.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language requirements for immigrants are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Closed-shop rules are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Heller's pluralism and personal faith views.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Heller said democracy needs safeguards and participation beyond procedure; split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from Heller's emphasis on personal autonomy and choosing yourself.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the school's opposition to state control of information.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design in this form is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Heller called the welfare state the best redistributive tool, which includes universal health services.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from Heller's support for the welfare state as the best redistributive tool; wage floors are not discussed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The school accepted the link between markets and freedom and the critique of planning but kept a critique of capitalism's logic. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

public-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the school accepted mixed economies.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from Heller's welfare redistribution support.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the school's support for independent organisation and the 1956 workers' revolution.

property-fundamental.rationale: Heller defended negative liberties but treated property as not absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Heller's critique of capitalist logic and consumer manipulation supports regulation; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Heller called the welfare state the best redistributive tool, though she criticised its individualism.

worker-ownership.rationale: Radical-needs thinking supports self-governance, but the school accepted market economies; split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The authors condemned totalitarian control of society; surveillance is inferred as unwelcome.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Heller defended negative liberties yet condemned racism; split.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from the school's distrust of state coercion.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sex work is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

decide-locally.rationale: Radical needs involve self-governance, but Heller held that modern states need representation and safeguards; split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the school's dignity-centred ethics; penal policy itself is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from Heller's autonomy and equality commitments.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the autonomy and equality commitments.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from Heller's emphasis on personal autonomy; abortion itself is not discussed in the sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred from the secular modern outlook of the school and Heller's pluralism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from Heller's ethics of equality and Holocaust-rooted moral inquiry; remedies are not discussed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The constructedness of gender is not discussed in the sources; Heller's critical stance on some feminism leaves it open.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism but valued culture as such; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Heller said no political revolution is needed yet defended the 1956 revolution; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from Heller's open society and anti-nationalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The school's writings give no clear view on the powers of the UN; neutral.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

nation-first.rationale: Heller criticised nationalism, so putting national interest ahead of global cooperation is rejected.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Heller held nations have a right not to be interfered with yet valued human rights; split.

open-borders.rationale: Border policy is not discussed in the sources; Heller's open-society outlook is offset by her view that nations hold rights.

limit-growth.rationale: Heller's needs theory distinguishes essential from artificial needs but she did not call for limits; split.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from Heller's concern with scarcity and polluting production; climate policy itself is not discussed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Heller held modernity is a paradox that cannot be solved and criticised the technological imagination.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

revolution-justified.rationale: Heller called 1956 the only truly socialist revolution but said after 1968 no political revolution is needed. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

experts-over-public.rationale: Heller objected to officials or experts defining people's 'real needs' for them, which leans against expert authority; she does not address how policy decisions should be weighted between experts and the public.

central-planning.rationale: The authors argued that Soviet-type planning was inefficient by design and dismissed the idea that such regimes were rational, and accepted critiques of planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The school accepted markets and a mixed economy; adherents would accept markets with social or worker ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is not discussed in the sources on the school; neutral.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Heller held that revolution can be justified (1956) and nations have rights, so an absolute ban on initiating force is not her position, though she opposed violence as policy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession conflicts with the democratic selection of rulers central to the school's politics.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Heller defended constitutional safeguards and rights against arbitrary rule, which implies public standing laws.

women-suffrage.rationale: The school held that socialism cannot exist without democracy, rights and pluralism, and Heller's radical-democratic philosophy takes equal political rights as basic.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the school's focus on alienation and needs under modernity rather than religion; Heller was critical of dogma but never argued this specifically.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its humanist, anti-essentialist outlook and later radical-democratic stance; the sources do not discuss race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the later members accepted the welfare state and constitutional rights but were wary of state paternalism over needs.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist humanist critique of property and the stress on needs over ownership; no source discusses original appropriation.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Heller's post-Marxist commitment to constitutional rights and her opposition to totalitarian rulers; no source discusses international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from Heller's secular, modernist ethics, which treat moral norms as human and plural rather than revealed; no source discusses scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from Heller's feminism and commitment to equal rights and participation, noted in her biography, and from the school's pluralist democracy.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The school condemned Soviet-type planned societies as totalitarian dictatorships over needs, so they would not defend such a state for its economic system.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the school's radical democracy and demand for popular participation, which favours direct choice of leaders; indirect council systems are not discussed.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from Heller's pluralism and constitutional rights, which favour equal treatment of religions; no source addresses national churches.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Heller was sympathetic to cultural pluralism but wary of nationalism, and no source takes a position on ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the school's radical-democratic commitment to people deciding their own affairs; no source discusses plebiscites on territory.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The question is outside the school's work, and its democratic and anti-nationalist strands point in opposite directions.

simple-living.rationale: The school criticised consumer society but defended a rich plurality of radical needs, not self-sufficiency or limited needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the school's liberal-democratic rights and freedom of movement; no source discusses indigenous homelands.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from Heller's feminism and commitment to equal rights; no source discusses conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from Heller's critical stance on nationalism.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Heller endorses constitutional rights and the rule of law and condemns totalitarian dictatorship over needs.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from the school's critique of Soviet-type societies and its commitment to democracy; no source discusses China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Heller's critique of nationalism; no source discusses kin minorities.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the school's egalitarian humanism and radical needs theory; no source discusses compensation for appropriation.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Heller's endorsement of liberal rights and the humanist emphasis on individual self-determination.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the sources give no tax-structure views.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: Heller backs the welfare state but the sources do not discuss targeting versus universality.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The authors hold that socialism needs democracy and pluralism, so bypassing parties and groups is rejected.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the later acceptance of markets under constitutional rights; not discussed directly.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from Heller's liberal pluralism and modernity ethics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: Heller's ethics of modernity embraces modernity rather than a return to ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from Heller's feminism and commitment to equal rights, as described on her page.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the school's radical-needs egalitarianism, which judges distribution by needs rather than only by origin.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: Heller favours redistribution and welfare tools; no source discusses this tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from Heller's equality commitments and campaigning; no source discusses the statement.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from Heller's moral universalism and rights-based ethics.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Márkus's critique of the labour paradigm and the focus on freeing needs beyond work.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Márkus criticised the labour paradigm, and the school largely abandoned orthodox Marxist economics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from Heller's critique of nationalism and the school's universalist humanism.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: radical needs theory covers cultural and personal needs, not workers' material interests alone.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The authors condemn party-led Soviet-type societies as totalitarian and insist socialism cannot exist without democracy.

missingStatements.text: No party or state should decide what people's real needs are.
missingStatements.rationale: The school's central charge against Soviet-type regimes was a 'dictatorship over needs', and Heller said she would not tolerate anyone telling her what her real needs were.
The review reports that the authors made the link between socialism and democracy central, holding socialism inconceivable without democracy.
missingStatements.declined: Covered loosely by person-over-state; the socialism-needs-democracy link is specific to socialist traditions and already reflected in democracy-best and socialism-needs-workers-power.

notes: Members diverged after exile: Heller and Fehér moved toward post-Marxist liberal democracy, while Márkus kept more of the Marxist framework. Many associates abandoned Marxism entirely. Policy answers are mostly inferred from principle.
